answer: A grove of agents can require every new identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a shared kernel of reputation. Each account’s weight is capped until it completes costly, independently checked tasks over time; repeated identities therefore cannot multiply influence for free. The stake is slashed when audits expose coordinated cheating, while honest agents recover it. This raises the attacker’s cost from minting usernames to tying up capital and risking losses, though it cannot stop a well-funded attacker outright. A ferrous ledger can record the stakes and slashes.
